outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the hypersurface conjecture is still open in full. Partial results have appeared for closed minimal hypersurfaces in S^5 (n=4) and S^6 (n=5), each adding a constant-invariant hypothesis; the second-gap constant has moved (for constant scalar curvature, S>n now forces S>1.4557n, 4 Oct 2026); and S>=2n was proved under an added constant cubic-trace hypothesis (22 Sep 2026). A higher-codimension version was disproved (18 Aug 2026), but the abstract's ranges exclude hypersurfaces. No AI system is credited with any hypersurface result in this record.
problem_asks: The bullet names one conjecture, 'Chern's conjecture for hypersurfaces in spheres', and adds 'a number of closely related conjectures' without listing them, so the statement alone does not enumerate the parts. The list below comes from the Wikipedia article the bullet links (current revision, fetched 11 Oct 2026; the frozen January 2024 text was not checked and may differ). (1) Discreteness, posed by Chern and listed as problem 105 in Yau's 1982 problem list: for closed minimal hypersurfaces M^n in the unit sphere S^{n+1} with constant scalar curvature, is the set of attained scalar-curvature values discrete? Since R = n(n-1) - S for a minimal hypersurface, this is the same as asking whether the attained values of S = squared norm of the second fundamental form form a discrete set. (2) Isoparametric (strong) form: must every such closed hypersurface with constant scalar curvature be isoparametric? (3) Strongest form, as the article words it: if S lies in an interval between thresholds a_k, the hypersurface is isoparametric and S takes an endpoint value; if S >= a_5 then S = a_5. (4) Second gap: S > n forces S >= 2n (the article's threshold case). (5) Lu's variant (2008): for minimal submanifolds of codimension m, replace S by S + lambda_2, where lambda_2 is the second-largest eigenvalue of the matrix of inner products of the shape operators; if the constant exceeds n it exceeds n + eps(n,m). (6) Chern's original question (the article's first formulation): for closed minimal submanifolds of the unit sphere of arbitrary codimension with constant second-fundamental-form length sigma, is the set of possible sigma values discrete, and what is the infimum of sigma values above n/(2 - 1/m)? (7) Bryant's conjecture: a piece of a minimal hypersurface of S^4 with constant scalar curvature, not assumed closed, is isoparametric of type g <= 3.

events.what_happened: C. K. Peng and C. L. Terng, second-pinching work for closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature in S^{n+1}: S > n forces S above n by a fixed gap (the search sources give 1/(12n); they disagree on the endpoint). For n=3 the value S=6 is sharp. Cited in a 2026 search snippet as Math. Ann. 266 (1983) 105-113 and Annals of Math. Studies 103 (1983) 177-198. Neither paper was opened; the Wikipedia article (opened) dates a related Peng-Terng pinching problem to 1983.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources only (not read): for closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant S, S > n implies S >= n + 1/(12n) (endpoint disputed across sources), with n=3 sharp at S=6. Restricted to a gap above n; it does not give discreteness or isoparametricity for any n.
events.remains: Discreteness of the S values for all n; isoparametricity for all n; the second gap S >= 2n for n >= 4.
events.doubts: The endpoint of the gap differs between the sources seen, and the original papers were not read.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjectured conclusion: a gap above n exists for constant-S hypersurfaces, and the n=3 gap is sharp.

events.what_happened: Shaoping Chang, 'On minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvatures in S^4', J. Differential Geom. 37(3) (1993) 523-534, DOI 10.4310/jdg/1214453898. The bibliographic record was opened; the article text was not available. Secondary statements in 2026 search snippets and a 2008 survey (none of which were read in full) say this paper completes the strong (isoparametric) form for closed minimal hypersurfaces of S^4 with constant scalar curvature, that is the n=3 case. One snippet says the Bryant local conjecture is verified only when M^3 has multiple principal curvatures somewhere. Chang's related 1993 and 1994 papers were seen only in snippets.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources only (unverified): a closed minimal M^3 in S^4 with constant scalar curvature is isoparametric, with 1, 2 or 3 distinct principal curvatures. That settles the n=3 case of the isoparametric form, and with it discreteness. Restricted to n=3 in S^4. The local Bryant case is partial only, per the same sources.
events.remains: All n >= 4; Bryant's local conjecture in general.

checked_by.who: Journal of Differential Geometry (refereed journal), volume 37 issue 3
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the article. Referee reports are not public. The article text was not read by this run.

events.doubts: The n=3 claim is attributed to Chang in secondary sources, while one search snippet attributes the strong n=3 result to Peng and Terng. The paper itself was not read.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjectured conclusion for n=3 (isoparametric, discrete values), per secondary sources.

events.what_happened: Hongwei Xu and Zhiyuan Xu, 'New result on Chern conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces and its application', arXiv:1605.07250 (24 May 2016, single version). Abstract read: for a compact minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1} with 0 <= |A|^2 - n <= n/22, |A|^2 = n and M is a Clifford torus. The abstract also has a self-shrinker result, which is outside this bullet.
events.delivers: A gap of width n/22 above n for compact minimal hypersurfaces. The abstract does not assume constant S. The only value it fixes is S = n, the Clifford torus.
events.remains: Discreteness of S above n + n/22; isoparametricity; the second gap S >= 2n.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjectured gap near n.

events.what_happened: Li Lei, Hongwei Xu and Zhiyuan Xu, 'On Chern's conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres', arXiv:1712.01175 (4 Dec 2017, single version). Abstract read: a compact minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1} with 0 <= S - n <= n/18 has S = n and is a Clifford torus. The abstract says it verifies a rigidity theorem on the stronger version of Chern's conjecture.
events.delivers: A gap of width n/18 above n for compact minimal hypersurfaces, improving the n/22 constant. The abstract does not assume constant S. Only the value S = n is fixed.
events.remains: Discreteness above n + n/18; isoparametricity; the second gap.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjectured gap near n.

events.what_happened: Zizhou Tang, Dongyi Wei and Wenjiao Yan, 'A sufficient condition for a hypersurface to be isoparametric', arXiv:1803.10006 (27 Mar 2018, single version). Abstract read: on a closed manifold with nonnegative integral of scalar curvature, a symmetric tensor A with n distinct eigenvalues and constant tr(A^k) for k=1..n-1 has constant eigenvalues. Applied to the second fundamental form of a closed hypersurface of S^{n+1}, the arXiv abstract says this gives 'affirmative evidence to Chern's conjecture'. Journal version (Tohoku Math. J. 72(4), 2020) seen in a search snippet, not opened.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; journal version 2020 per snippet.
events.delivers: Isoparametricity for closed hypersurfaces under constant tr(h^k) for k=1..n-1 (all low-order power sums of the second fundamental form) and a nonnegative integral of scalar curvature. Restricted to those hypotheses; does not reach constant scalar curvature alone.
events.remains: Closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature and no further trace conditions; discreteness.
events.direction: Cuts toward the isoparametric conclusion under extra trace hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Jianquan Ge and Fagui Li, 'Integral-Einstein hypersurfaces in spheres', arXiv:2101.03753 (v1 11 Jan 2021; v3 28 Oct 2025). The arXiv comment says it was accepted by Communications in Analysis and Geometry on 15 Aug 2025. The abstract fragments read were: minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature in unit spheres, which are conjectured to be isoparametric in the Chern conjecture; 'IE' (integral-Einstein) hypersurfaces; and that minimal isoparametric hypersurfaces with g >= 3 are IE. The theorems were not read.
events.revisions: v1 11 Jan 2021; v3 28 Oct 2025 (content of the revision not read).
events.delivers: Per abstract fragments only: introduces the IE subclass of minimal constant-scalar-curvature hypersurfaces and records that minimal isoparametric hypersurfaces with g >= 3 belong to it. The abstract does not state a resolution of any part of the conjecture.
events.remains: Whether constant-scalar-curvature hypersurfaces are IE or isoparametric in general.

checked_by.who: Communications in Analysis and Geometry (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the article on 15 Aug 2025, per the arXiv comment field. Referee reports are not public.

events.direction: Background to the isoparametric side; it does not say which way the conjecture goes.

events.what_happened: Qing-Ming Cheng, Guoxin Wei and Takuya Yamashiro, 'Chern conjecture on minimal hypersurfaces', arXiv:2104.14057 (29 Apr 2021, single version). Abstract read: a complete minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere with constant scalar curvature and constant f_3 is a totally geodesic sphere or a Clifford torus when S <= 1.8252n - 0.712898.
events.delivers: Rigidity below the pinching threshold 1.8252n - 0.712898, for constant scalar curvature and constant f_3 (cubic trace). Restricted to that hypothesis and to values of S below the threshold.
events.remains: Values of S above 1.8252n - 0.712898; the case without constant f_3; discreteness; isoparametricity.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjectured rigidity below a threshold, under the constant-f_3 hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Pengpeng Cheng and Tongzhu Li, 'Rigidity of closed minimal hypersurface in S^5', arXiv:2410.19531 (v1 25 Oct 2024; no later version listed on the abstract page). Abstract read: for a closed immersed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant squared norm S, if the third mean curvature H_3 and the number g of distinct principal curvatures are both constant, then M^4 is isoparametric and S can only be 0, 4 or 12. Journal: a repository record seen in search (not opened) gives Differential Geometry and its Applications vol. 100 (2025), article 102252, DOI 10.1016/j.difgeo.2025.102252. The DOI redirect was observed; the Elsevier page was not read.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 25 Oct 2024 only; journal version Sept 2025 per repository snippet.
events.delivers: For closed minimal hypersurfaces with n=4 in S^5, under constant S together with constant H_3 and constant g: isoparametric, with S in {0, 4, 12}. The hypotheses H_3 and g are additional constancy assumptions.
events.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant S but without constant H_3 or g; all other n; the strong and second-gap forms.

checked_by.who: Differential Geometry and its Applications (Elsevier), journal of record
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the article, vol. 100 (Sept 2025), according to a repository record seen in search. Referee reports are not public.

events.direction: Toward the conjecture's conclusion: under the constancy hypotheses, the hypersurface is isoparametric with S in {0, 4, 12}.

events.what_happened: Joel Spruck and Ling Xiao, 'Closed minimal hypersurfaces in S^5 with constant S and A_3', arXiv:2503.23194 (29 Mar 2025, single version). Abstract read: for a closed minimally immersed M^4 in S^5 with S and A_3 constant and nonnegative scalar curvature R_M, M is isoparametric and S can only be 0, 4 or 12. No journal version was found.
events.delivers: For closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant S, under constant A_3 (sum of cubes of principal curvatures) and R_M >= 0: isoparametric, with S in {0, 4, 12}. For minimal M^4 in S^5 R = 12 - S, so the sign condition R_M >= 0 amounts to S <= 12 (my reading).
events.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant S and without constant A_3 or without the sign condition; other n.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture's conclusion, under the constant A_3 and sign hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Reiko Miyaoka, 'Chern's Conjecture in the Dupin case', arXiv:2504.02621 (3 Apr 2025, single version). Abstract read: a closed proper Dupin hypersurface with constant mean curvature is isoparametric (i) if g=3, (ii) if g=4 and constant scalar curvature, (iii) if g=4 and constant Lie curvature, or (iv) if g=6 and constant Lie curvatures; the abstract says these cover all non-trivial cases. The paper's open questions were read: whether a closed minimal or CMC hypersurface with g=4 and constant scalar curvature must be Dupin, and the analogous question for constant Lie curvature. A search snippet says the manuscript was received by the Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan on 16 Oct 2025; that PDF could not be read.
events.delivers: Isoparametricity for closed proper Dupin hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature (which includes minimal) under one of the four conditions (i) to (iv). The conclusion is restricted to Dupin hypersurfaces.
events.remains: Closed minimal hypersurfaces that are not Dupin; whether constant scalar curvature with g=4 forces the Dupin property (the author's open question); g=6 with constant scalar curvature (the author suspects a negative answer).

checked_by.qualification: Machine-written review site, not a human reading
checked_by.what_they_did: A machine-written summary of the paper, seen in search. The page itself returned HTTP 429 on fetch and was not read.

events.direction: Toward the isoparametric conclusion, but only for the Dupin class.

events.what_happened: Jianquan Ge, Huixin Tan, Wenjiao Yan and Yunheng Zhang, 'Chern Conjecture on Minimal Willmore Hypersurfaces with Constant Scalar Curvature', arXiv:2512.08342 (9 Dec 2025, single version; 12 pages per comment). Abstract read: for a closed minimal Willmore hypersurface M^n of S^{n+1} with constant scalar curvature, if S > n then S >= n + (4n + 9 - sqrt(4n^2 + 60n + 81))/2. The abstract says this proves, 'in the approximate sense', the Chern conjecture about the second gap, and that the full statement 'will be fully verified under a further inequality condition about the 4-th mean curvature' (the condition is not given in the abstract). The bound is approximately 2n - 3 for large n (my arithmetic).
events.delivers: For the Willmore subclass with constant scalar curvature: S > n forces S above n + (4n+9 - sqrt(4n^2+60n+81))/2, about 2n - 3. The abstract describes this as an approximate proof of the second gap; the full second gap is conditional on an unstated inequality.
events.remains: The full second gap S >= 2n for the Willmore subclass, which the authors say needs an additional inequality; all non-Willmore closed minimal hypersurfaces.
events.doubts: The result is conditional: the full second-gap statement is said to need a further inequality on the fourth mean curvature, which is not given in the abstract. The preprint has not been reviewed as far as searches found.
events.direction: Cuts toward the second gap (S >= 2n) but does not reach it in the abstract's statement.

events.what_happened: Weiran Ding, Jianquan Ge, Fagui Li and Xize Yang, 'Lu's conjecture for minimal surfaces', arXiv:2601.07194 (12 Jan 2026, single version; 21 pages). Abstract read: proves Lu's conjecture for minimal 2-spheres in arbitrary codimension, and for any minimal surfaces under 'slight inequality conditions about the normal scalar curvature'. Chern's conjecture appears only as background.
events.delivers: Lu's second-gap variant (S + lambda_2) for minimal surfaces: all minimal 2-spheres in any codimension, and surfaces under a normal-scalar-curvature inequality. This is a variant from the article's list, for surfaces (n=2) not hypersurfaces of general dimension.
events.remains: Lu's variant for surfaces without the inequality; Lu's variant for minimal submanifolds of dimension n >= 3; the hypersurface conjecture.
events.direction: Cuts toward Lu's conjectured second gap, for surfaces only.

events.what_happened: Chengchao He, Hongwei Xu and Entao Zhao, 'Classification of closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature in S^5', arXiv:2603.01181 (1 Mar 2026, single version; 20 pages). Abstract read: a closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature and constant 3rd mean curvature is isoparametric, and is one of an equatorial S^4, S^2(sqrt2/2) x S^2(sqrt2/2), S^1(1/2) x S^3(sqrt3/2), or a Cartan minimal hypersurface. The abstract page has no AI or acknowledgement statement.
events.delivers: For closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature and constant 3rd mean curvature: isoparametric, in one of four listed types. The title says 'classification', but the classification depends on the constant-H_3 hypothesis.
events.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature and without constant 3rd mean curvature; other n.
events.direction: Toward the isoparametric conclusion under the constant 3rd-mean-curvature hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Davide Dameno and Aaron J. Tyrrell, 'Topological and rigidity results for four-dimensional hypersurfaces in space forms', arXiv:2603.03775 (v1 4 Mar 2026; v2 29 Apr 2026). Abstract read (the page gives only the abstract): for closed minimal hypersurfaces M^4 in 5-dimensional space forms, Weyl-functional bounds and second-fundamental-form estimates in the minimal constant-scalar-curvature case, with an Euler-characteristic bound for constant non-negative sectional curvature ambient, under a cross-sectional area assumption. The abstract says the work is 'inspired by' Chern's conjecture and the second pinching problem, and does not claim to prove it.
events.revisions: v1 4 Mar 2026; v2 29 Apr 2026 ('improved the statement of Theorem 1.13 and added Corollary 1.17').
events.delivers: Estimates for |A|^2 and the Weyl functional, and a topological bound, for minimal constant-scalar-curvature M^4 in 5-dimensional space forms, under an area assumption. This is not a classification or a discreteness result as far as the abstract shows. Full theorem statements were not read.
events.remains: Discreteness of the S values; isoparametricity; the case without the area assumption.
events.doubts: The theorems were not read; the abstract page does not give the exact hypotheses of Theorem 1.13.
events.direction: Estimates, not a verdict on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Ya Tao, 'Minimal Hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature in S^6', arXiv:2605.19495 (v1 19 May 2026; v4 30 Jul 2026). Abstract read: for a closed minimal hypersurface M^5 in S^6, under constant S, f_3 and f_4, M is isoparametric; a point with exactly two distinct principal curvatures forces a Clifford torus. The abstract says it removes the nonnegative scalar curvature assumption used by Tang and Yan. The theorem statements were not read.
events.revisions: v1 19 May 2026; v2 20 May; v3 21 May; v4 30 Jul 2026.
events.delivers: For closed minimal hypersurfaces with n=5 in S^6, under constant S, f_3 and f_4: isoparametric. Also a rigidity statement (Clifford torus) for a point with exactly two distinct principal curvatures.
events.remains: Closed minimal M^5 in S^6 without constant f_3 and f_4; other n.
events.doubts: Single-author preprint, not reviewed as far as searches found. The theorem statements were not read.
events.direction: Toward the isoparametric conclusion under constant f_3 and f_4.

events.what_happened: Jianquan Ge, Tong Liu, Keyan Luo and Wenjiao Yan, 'Rigidity of Closed Minimal Hypersurfaces in S^5', arXiv:2606.29246 (28 Jun 2026, single version; 31 pages). Abstract read: the authors 'resolve this conjecture in the affirmative for M^4 in S^5' under the assumption that the Gauss-Kronecker curvature K is constant. Theorem 1.1 (read via the HTML rendering): if S and K are constant then M is isoparametric, with three cases according to the sign of K. The introduction, as rendered, notes that for minimal M^4 with constant S, constant K is equivalent to constant P_4. The HTML was read to character 100,000 of about 115,000.
events.delivers: For closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant S and constant Gauss-Kronecker curvature K: isoparametric. For minimal M^4, constant S is the same as constant scalar curvature (R = 12 - S), so this is constant scalar curvature plus constant K (my reading).
events.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature but without constant K; other n.
events.doubts: The abstract and theorem both add constant K. The paper says it resolves a nonconsecutive-trace version rather than the conjecture as originally stated. Not reviewed as far as searches found.
events.direction: Toward the isoparametric conclusion under constant K.

events.what_happened: Fagui Li and Yuhang Zhao, 'Flat minimal tori and Lu's second-gap conjecture', arXiv:2606.30432 (v1 29 Jun 2026; v2 18 Aug 2026). Abstract read: 'We disprove this second-gap conjecture for minimal surfaces in every codimension q >= 3'. The abstract concerns Lu's S + lambda_2 quantity and does not mention Chern's conjecture.
events.delivers: A counterexample to Lu's second-gap conjecture, as stated for minimal surfaces, in codimension q >= 3. Hypersurfaces are excluded by q >= 3. The construction was not read.
events.remains: Lu's variant for hypersurfaces; codimension 2 surfaces; the hypersurface conjecture.
events.doubts: The construction was not read. Whether the disproof touches the article's Lu variant depends on how the variant is read for surfaces; that is for the judging pass.
events.direction: Cuts against Lu's variant, for surfaces in codimension >= 3 only.
events.object: Flat minimal tori (per the title) in codimension q >= 3 that the abstract says disprove Lu's second-gap conjecture for minimal surfaces. The explicit construction and the verification were not read.

events.what_happened: Qintao Deng and Yunjia Kou, 'Closed Minimal Hypersurfaces in S^5(1) with Constant Scalar and Gauss-Kronecker Curvatures', arXiv:2607.06588 (v1 5 Jul 2026; v2 9 Jul 2026; 34 pages main text, 8 appendix). Abstract read: any closed minimal M^4 of S^5(1) with constant scalar curvature and constant Gauss-Kronecker curvature must be isoparametric. The S values {0, 4, 12} come from a search snippet, not the fetched abstract. No acknowledgement or AI statement on the abstract page.
events.delivers: For closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature and constant Gauss-Kronecker curvature: isoparametric. The authors present this as strong support for the conjecture.
events.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature but without constant K; other n.
events.doubts: Same hypotheses as the Ge-Liu-Luo-Yan paper of 28 June 2026; the two papers were not checked against each other. Not reviewed as far as searches found.
events.direction: Toward the isoparametric conclusion under constant K.

events.what_happened: Jianquan Ge, Fagui Li and Yunheng Zhang, 'On Chern's Conjecture for Minimal Submanifolds with Flat Normal Bundle in Spheres', arXiv:2607.10733 (12 Jul 2026, single version; 43 pages). Abstract read: for a closed minimal M^n (n >= 3) in S^{n+m} (m >= 2) with flat normal bundle, if S is constant and 0 <= S <= n + delta with delta >= n/87, then either S = 0 and M is a totally geodesic sphere, or S = n and M is a Clifford torus.
events.delivers: A second-gap rigidity statement for minimal submanifolds of codimension m >= 2 with flat normal bundle and constant S, with delta >= n/87. Hypersurfaces are excluded by m >= 2.
events.remains: Hypersurfaces (m=1); codimension m >= 2 without the flat normal bundle; the second gap.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjectured rigidity, in higher codimension with flat normal bundle; not the hypersurface case.

events.what_happened: Fagui Li and Yuhang Zhao, 'A Curvature Gap for Minimal Submanifolds in Spheres', arXiv:2608.16095 (v1 17 Aug 2026; v2 18 Aug 2026; v3 8 Sep 2026). Abstract read: for a closed minimal immersion of M^n into S^{n+q}(1), n >= 3, q >= 2, not totally geodesic, max S exceeds an explicit bound that is above 2n/3 plus a constant times (n-2). The abstract page's comment field reads 'Using AI to provide better inequality estimates and improve constants'. The arXiv HTML rendering includes a 'Declaration of generative AI use' (quoted below). The PDF could not be read in WebFetch.
events.revisions: v1 17 Aug 2026; v2 18 Aug 2026; v3 8 Sep 2026 (the comment quoted is from the v3 abstract page).
events.delivers: A curvature gap for max S of closed minimal submanifolds of codimension q >= 2. Hypersurfaces are excluded by q >= 2. It is a gap on max S, not a statement about constant-S hypersurfaces.
events.remains: Hypersurfaces (q=1); the constant-S discreteness question; the second gap S >= 2n for hypersurfaces.
events.doubts: The AI declaration says computations were used 'only as auxiliary input' and were checked. The comment says the AI was used 'to provide better inequality estimates and improve constants', which is a load-bearing-sounding claim about the theorem's constants. The declaration says 'the author' though the arXiv record lists two authors. The quoted wording comes from a model-rendered WebFetch of the HTML and should be checked against the source.
events.direction: Cuts toward a curvature gap in codimension >= 2, not the hypersurface conjecture.

The comment field says the AI was used 'to provide better inequality estimates and improve constants'. Which estimates and constants are in the main theorem is not established.

AI-generated suggestions and computations were used only as auxiliary input ... were independently checked before being incorporated into the manuscript.' events.what_happened: Benjy Firester and Raphael Tsiamis, 'On Chern's conjecture for minimal submanifolds of the sphere', arXiv:2608.18074 (18 Aug 2026, single version; 5 pages). Abstract read: 'We disprove this conjecture for all n >= 3 with m >= 4, and for even n >= 4 with m >= 3'; the property 'holds in every codimension when n in {1, 2}'. The conjecture is that of Chern, do Carmo and Kobayashi: for closed minimal n-submanifolds of S^{n+m} with constant second-fundamental-form length, the scalar curvature takes values in a discrete set. The abstract page does not say whether m=1 is covered, but the stated ranges exclude it.
events.delivers: A negative answer to the general-codimension discreteness question (the article's first formulation, Chern's original question) for n >= 3 with m >= 4, and for even n >= 4 with m >= 3. Hypersurfaces (m=1) are not covered by the stated ranges, so the hypersurface conjecture is not disproved.
events.remains: The hypersurface discreteness and isoparametricity conjectures (m=1), which the abstract does not address; the codimension cases m=2, and m=3 for odd n >= 3, as far as the abstract says.
events.doubts: Single five-page preprint, not reviewed as far as searches found. The construction was not read. The article's first formulation is for general codimension, so whether this bears on the bullet is a scope question for the judging pass.
events.direction: Cuts against Chern's original general-codimension discreteness question for m >= 4 (and even n with m >= 3). Does not reach the hypersurface case as far as the abstract shows.
events.object: Counterexamples to the discreteness of constant-S scalar curvature for closed minimal submanifolds in codimension m >= 4 (n >= 3) or m >= 3 (n even >= 4). The construction was not read. A search snippet from an unopened ResearchGate page describes explicit minimal embeddings S^2 x S^1 into S^7, which would be n=3, m=4; that is unverified.

events.what_happened: Qintao Deng and Yunjia Kou, 'On the Rigidity of Closed CMC Hypersurfaces in S^5(1) with Constant Scalar Curvature', arXiv:2608.22311 (v1 23 Aug 2026; 21 pages). Abstract read: a closed CMC M^4 in S^5(1) with constant scalar curvature and constant third power sum f_3: if M^4 has exactly two distinct principal curvatures at some point, then it is isoparametric. The abstract also says every closed CMC Willmore hypersurface with constant scalar curvature is isoparametric. The minimal case (H=0) is included, with Clifford torus and Cartan conclusions.
events.delivers: For closed M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature and constant f_3: isoparametric if there is a point with exactly two distinct principal curvatures. Also isoparametric for the Willmore subclass. Minimal M^4 is included as H=0.
events.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant scalar curvature and without constant f_3 or the two-principal-curvature point; other n.
events.direction: Toward the isoparametric conclusion under the stated hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Li Lei, 'Rigidity of Minimal Submanifolds in Spheres of Higher Codimension', arXiv:2609.04393 (v1 3 Sep 2026). The abstract page says it investigates 'Chern's conjecture for minimal submanifolds of higher codimension in the unit sphere' and gives a rigidity theorem under a pinching condition on S. The theorem was not read.
events.delivers: A pinching rigidity theorem for minimal submanifolds of higher codimension. The abstract says it does not concern hypersurfaces. Exact statement not read.
events.remains: Hypersurfaces; the codimension-one conjecture.
events.direction: Higher codimension; not the hypersurface case.

events.what_happened: Ruihan Chen, 'An improved second pinching theorem for minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature in spheres', arXiv:2609.17586 (v1 10 Sep 2026; 14 pages). Abstract read: for closed minimal hypersurfaces M^n of the unit sphere with constant S and n >= 4, S > n implies S > 85n/59 (about 1.4407n), improving the 10n/7 of Suh and Yang. The abstract says no constancy assumption is imposed on the cubic trace f_3.
events.delivers: For closed minimal hypersurfaces with n >= 4 and constant S: S > n forces S > 85n/59. This moves the second-gap constant without assuming constant f_3. The bound is superseded by the Cheng-Li-Wei bound of 4 Oct 2026 (about 1.4557n).
events.remains: S >= 2n; discreteness; isoparametricity.
events.direction: Cuts toward the second gap (S >= 2n), with the constant moved to 85/59.

events.what_happened: Shanlin Guan, 'The Second Gap for Minimal Hypersurfaces in the Unit Sphere with Constant Cubic Trace', arXiv:2609.26852 (v1 22 Sep 2026; 13 pages). Abstract read: for a closed oriented minimal hypersurface M^n of the unit sphere, n >= 3, with constant scalar curvature and constant f_3 = tr(h^3): S > n implies S >= 2n, with equality exactly when each component is locally a Cartan minimal isoparametric hypersurface with three distinct principal curvatures.
events.delivers: The full second gap S >= 2n for closed minimal hypersurfaces with n >= 3 and constant scalar curvature, under the added hypothesis of constant f_3, with equality cases classified. The restriction to constant f_3 is part of the stated hypothesis.
events.remains: The second gap S >= 2n without constant f_3; discreteness; isoparametricity in general.
events.doubts: Single 13-page preprint, not reviewed as far as searches found. The proof was not read.
events.direction: Toward the second gap (S >= 2n) and toward the isoparametric conclusion, under constant f_3.

events.what_happened: Qing-Ming Cheng, Fengjiang Li and Guoxin Wei, 'An improved result on Chern conjecture', arXiv:2610.05276 (v1 4 Oct 2026). Read via the HTML rendering. Theorem 1.1: for a complete minimal hypersurface X: M^n -> S^{n+1}(1), n >= 4, with constant scalar curvature, if S > n then S > (10000000/6869671) n, which is above 1.4556737869 n and above n + (221/485) n. Remark 1.3 states S > (3/2) n for 4 <= n <= 13. No constant f_3 assumed.
events.delivers: For complete minimal hypersurfaces with n >= 4 and constant scalar curvature: S > n forces S > 1.4556737869 n. This moves the second-gap constant without assuming constant f_3. It does not reach 2n.
events.remains: S >= 2n for n >= 4; discreteness; isoparametricity.
events.doubts: Single preprint, one week old, not reviewed as far as searches found. The HTML rendering was read; the theorem was not checked by hand.
events.direction: Cuts toward the second gap (S >= 2n), with the constant moved to about 1.4557.

disputes.summary: Sources disagree on who proved the strong (isoparametric) form for n=3, closed minimal hypersurfaces in S^4. Some snippets credit Peng and Terng (1983) and others Chang (1993). Sources also differ on the endpoint of the Peng-Terng gap (1/(12n) in some; other values elsewhere). Neither original paper was read.

summary: Searched 40 queries and opened about 35 pages, covering the Wikipedia article (current revision), arXiv abstract and HTML pages, the Project Euclid record for Chang (1993), and AI-tracker and news results. Since 26 January 2024 the record holds 19 events. None settles the bullet for all dimensions. Partial results for the isoparametric and discreteness conjectures for closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature are: n=4 in S^5 (Cheng-Li 2024; Spruck-Xiao 2025; He-Xu-Zhao 2026; Ge-Liu-Luo-Yan 2026; Deng-Kou 2026), each adding a constant invariant (H_3, A_3 with a sign condition, a 3rd mean curvature, K, or a constant f_3 with a two-principal-curvature point); n=5 in S^6 (Tao 2026, constant f_3 and f_4); and the Dupin class in any dimension (Miyaoka 2025). None of these removes the extra hypothesis, as far as the abstracts or the readable text show. The second-gap family moved in 2026. For constant scalar curvature with n >= 4, S > n now forces S > 1.4557n (Cheng-Li-Wei, 4 Oct 2026), improving Chen's 85n/59 (10 Sep 2026), which had improved Suh-Yang's 10n/7. For n >= 3 with constant f_3, Guan (22 Sep 2026) proves S > n forces S >= 2n with equality classified; the Willmore subclass gets an approximate bound near 2n-3 (Ge-Tan-Yan-Zhang, Dec 2025) with the full statement conditional. Higher-codimension statements were disproved or extended: Firester-Tsiamis (18 Aug 2026) disprove the general-codimension discreteness question for m >= 4 (and even n with m >= 3), and Li-Zhao (29 Jun 2026) disprove Lu's second-gap conjecture for minimal surfaces in codimension >= 3. Those ranges exclude hypersurfaces. Close calls: (a) Firester-Tsiamis is a negative answer to the article's first formulation, which is for general codimension, while the bullet is titled for hypersurfaces; the record reads the abstract's ranges as excluding m=1. (b) Guan's S >= 2n uses constant f_3, which is an added hypothesis; it is the second-gap statement itself, but with the extra assumption. (c) The Dupin result of Miyaoka covers only Dupin hypersurfaces, and the step from constant scalar curvature to Dupin is listed by the author as open. (d) The Ge-Tan-Yan-Zhang result is conditional, and the authors say the full statement needs an inequality on the fourth mean curvature that is not stated in the abstract. Scope calls were made by reading each abstract's hypotheses against the bullet; the bullet's own statement names no sub-conjectures, so the enumeration in problem_asks comes from the Wikipedia article. AI: no AI system is credited with any hypersurface result found. The only AI disclosure on a related item is Li-Zhao 2608.16095 (a curvature gap in codimension q >= 2, which excludes hypersurfaces). Its declaration names OpenAI's ChatGPT, including its Codex tools, for polishing, LaTeX, computations and checks, and its comment says AI was used 'to provide better inequality estimates and improve constants'. Whether that touches the main theorem is not established. Other AI-tagged items found are not this problem: 2607.27444 and 2607.29632 (opened; their abstract pages show no AI statement and their topics are not sphere CSC); 2608.27398 (a GPT-5.6 Ultra disclosure in area-minimizing hypercones; snippet only); the OpenAI unit-distance counterexample (discrete geometry); a crypto-news report of Claude and the complex structure on S^6 (a different problem, unverified, not opened); and the Erdos and FrontierMath results. Human checking is thin. Most 2024-2026 results are arXiv preprints without review found. Refereed publication is documented only for Cheng-Li (Differential Geometry and its Applications, Sept 2025, from a repository record; the Elsevier page was not read), Chang (1993, bibliographic record only), and Ge-Li 2021 (accepted by CAG on 15 Aug 2025, per the arXiv comment). A Miyaoka manuscript is marked as submitted to JMSJ per a search snippet. No Lean formalisation, no expert blog digest, and no Quanta or Tao coverage was found for any of these results. Several PDFs could not be read through WebFetch (Scherfner-Weiss 2008, Chang 1993 text, Peng-Terng, the Cheng-Li journal page, the Miyaoka JMSJ PDF, and the 2608.16095 PDF), so claims attributed to them come from search snippets and are labelled as such. The 2608.16095 AI quotes are from a model-rendered WebFetch of the HTML and should be checked against the source.
competing_reading: (1) Read the n=4 S^5 papers together: each adds a constant invariant, and a reader might take the union as covering closed minimal M^4 with constant scalar curvature, since they are all in the same setting. The sources do not show that they cover it, so this reading is weak. (2) Read Firester-Tsiamis (18 Aug 2026) as a negative answer to a named member of the article's family (Chern's original question). A judge who counts a negative answer to any listed member as moving the bullet would record a disproof here, while the hypersurface case is untouched. (3) Read Guan's S >= 2n under constant f_3 as the second-gap conjecture itself for n >= 3, since the equality cases match Cartan's examples. The added f_3 hypothesis is what keeps it from being general. (4) Read Lu's variant as part of the bullet, in which case Li-Zhao's flat tori (2026-06) and Ding-Ge-Li-Yang (2026-01) are events on it, though both concern surfaces.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The frozen January 2024 text of the bullet and of the article it links, to see which sub-conjectures it lists, since the current article was used here. (b) The full text of 2608.18074 to confirm that the stated ranges exclude m=1, and of 2606.30432 to confirm that q >= 3 excludes hypersurfaces. (c) The full text of 2603.01181, 2606.29246, 2607.06588, 2608.22311, 2503.23194 and 2605.19495 to confirm that no step removes the constant-invariant hypotheses. (d) The proof in 2609.26852, to see whether constant f_3 is essential there. (e) Chang 1993 and Peng-Terng 1983, to confirm the n=3 attribution and the exact gap. (f) Referee reports or expert write-ups for any of the 2026 preprints. (g) For the AI question, the PDF of 2608.16095: whether the declaration's inequality work appears in the main theorem, and which named system produced it.
incomplete: (1) The statement names no sub-conjectures, so problem_asks uses the Wikipedia article's current revision (fetched 11 Oct 2026), not the frozen January 2024 text. (2) Most arXiv items were read through abstract pages only; full theorems were read for Ge-Liu-Luo-Yan (HTML to character 100,000 of about 115,000), Cheng-Li-Wei (HTML) and 2608.16095 (HTML, declaration only). (3) Not read in full: Chang 1993 (only the bibliographic record); Peng-Terng 1983 (cited via snippets only); the Scherfner-Weiss 2008 PDF (unreadable through WebFetch); the Cheng-Li journal page (DOI redirect observed, page not read); the Miyaoka JMSJ PDF (unreadable); the themoonlight review (HTTP 429). (4) 2608.16095's PDF returned binary through WebFetch, so the AI declaration rests on the HTML rendering. (5) The Deng-Kou S values {0,4,12} for 2607.06588 come from a search snippet, not the fetched abstract. (6) Seen only in search results and not opened: 2609.04631 (high-codimension pinching), 2609.13949 (local CMC rigidity, Bryant mention), 2609.12152 (taut and Dupin survey), 1008.3683 (Chern conjecture and isoparametric hypersurfaces), 2001.10134 (Tang-Yan 2020, CMC case), 2104.08104 (dimension-four note), 1012.1073 (Some results on Chern's problem, 2010), 2109.11768, 2605.25271, 2605.26234, 2603.18813, 2608.27398, and the 2026 Chinese survey by Cheng and Wei (Scientia Sinica Mathematica 2025, DOI 10.1360/SSM-2024-0077). (7) The journal status of Spruck-Xiao, Deng-Kou (both), Miyaoka, Ge-Tan-Yan-Zhang, Chen, Guan and Cheng-Li-Wei is not established. (8) Pre-2024 events were recorded only where the abstract or bibliographic page was read, or where a source for them was seen; there may be other pre-2024 partial results on this family that the searches did not reach. (9) No zbMATH or MathSciNet review was found; those databases were not queried directly. (10) The searches did not cover Google Scholar or the arXiv listing itself, and no arXiv search was run for the author names beyond the results found.

event.what_happened: Pengpeng Cheng and Tongzhu Li, 'Rigidity of closed minimal hypersurface in S^5', arXiv:2410.19531 (v1 25 Oct 2024; no later version listed on the abstract page). Abstract read: for a closed immersed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant squared norm S, if the third mean curvature H_3 and the number g of distinct principal curvatures are both constant, then M^4 is isoparametric and S can only be 0, 4 or 12. Journal: a repository record seen in search (not opened) gives Differential Geometry and its Applications vol. 100 (2025), article 102252, DOI 10.1016/j.difgeo.2025.102252. The DOI redirect was observed; the Elsevier page was not read.

event.remains: Closed minimal M^4 in S^5 with constant S but without constant H_3 or g; all other n; the strong and second-gap forms.

judgement.why: The statement is explicitly a family ('a number of closely related conjectures'), so nothing here is whole. Results proving isoparametricity for closed minimal constant-scalar-curvature hypersurfaces under an extra constancy hypothesis (constant H_3, A_3, K, f_3, Dupin) restrict the class of objects within the conjecture's own setting and are scored case rather than variant. Second-gap constant improvements (Chen, Cheng-Li-Wei, Willmore approximate bound) are bound. Firester-Tsiamis refutes Chern's original general-codimension discreteness question, a named member of the family, so it is a case with refuted direction and counterexample; Li-Zhao's flat tori likewise refute Lu's listed variant for surfaces in codimension >= 3. Higher-codimension pinching results under different hypotheses (flat normal bundle, max S gap, Lei) are variant. Cheng-Li 2024 is digested via journal publication. The only AI disclosure (Li-Zhao 2608.16095) says AI provided 'better inequality estimates and improve constants', which is mathematics in the result, so assisted; that event is a variant regardless.
judgement.doubts: Whether Firester-Tsiamis and Li-Zhao flat tori bear on the bullet depends on counting the Wikipedia article's general-codimension and Lu formulations as part of 'closely related conjectures'; the January 2024 article text was not checked. Treating added-constancy-hypothesis results as case rather than variant is a close call. The 2608.16095 AI quote comes from a model-rendered fetch and the declaration otherwise describes AI as auxiliary; assisted vs none is close.
